title: press-office-probes-report-to-the-watch
intention: Every standing WATCHME probe berthed in press_office reports to harbor_master's watch verb with {ticket, holds, finding} stated against its own ticket's falsifier, and each spec names that receiver.
why: Every standing probe in press_office mails with no verb and nothing uses it (835b5736bf2b D2); a88d6a368cfb built the watch verb that uses a WATCHME finding and 8ecb99998254 built watch_carry. Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: build the receivers.
traces_to: 835b5736bf2b's falsifier (zero probe-bearing standing specs lack a receiver) and Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a; the 2026-09-30 ruling that a probe's data must have a consumer that USES it; RULE 1 (the build stays inside press_office; base's helper through its public interface, harbor_master through its bus verb)
how: Measured 2026-10-04: 1 tickets at a rest carry a watchme probe under press_office/probes/ (eba8503cc18c). Read 2026-10-04: one standing ticket (eba8503cc18c, at PROVED) carries a probe under press_office/probes, concept_piece_voyages_journal, posting to='press_office' (a component with no device on the bus, so nothing reads that address) with no verb. Its trigger is count-shaped (>= 1 concept-piece@v1 crossing in press_office/history.json) and its enough is >= 3. No proof imports it (grep -rln 'concept_piece_voyages_journal|press_office.probes|press_office/probes' --include=*.py over the repo, 2026-10-04: no file). Each PROBE gets verb='watch' and carry=watch_carry(<its id>, _carry, <its predicate>), importing watch_carry from cairn.tools.base.probe (declared public). 1 post to='press_office' (eba8503cc18c) and retarget to='harbor_master'. Each ticket's watchme spec gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} through the artifact door. A proof under press_office/proofs reads the population from the commons and asserts each probe's verb, to, and live payload invariants.
falsifier: GREEN when every ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme.probe sits under press_office has a probe whose PROBE posts verb 'watch' to 'harbor_master' and whose payload over live data carries ticket == that ticket's id, holds a bool, and a non-empty finding whenever holds is False; and every such spec names receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} with watchme_spec_error naming no receiver fault. RED if any standing press_office spec lacks the receiver, or if a converted payload's ticket is a path or another id, or if a probe still posts to press_office. WRONG INTENT if a press_office probe's data has a reader other than its own ticket's FIXME that only Akien could name.
watchme: none, because what this child's probes say is read by harbor_master's watch verb (a88d6a368cfb, PROVED), and whether they ever fire is 164da559823d's and acb4ecd84364's watch (CairnCommons/tickets/164da559823d-*.json); a probe on probes reporting would need a receiver of its own.
children: none, because the change is 1 PROBE declarations and their specs, all inside press_office.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which probes and how: eba8503cc18c concept_piece_voyages_journal (holds=_holds). In each file under press_office/probes/: append watch_carry to the existing 'from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...' line; use the probe's id constant (named per probe below, added as `_TICKET_ID = "<id>"` after the import block when absent); in PROBE = Probe(...) replace 'carry=_carry,' with 'verb="watch",' and 'carry=watch_carry(<const>, _carry, <pred>),'. For concept_piece_voyages_journal also change to="press_office" to to="harbor_master". concept_piece_voyages_journal already holds _TICKET = "eba8503cc18c" (the 12-hex id), which watch_carry takes as its ticket; no constant is added. Its trigger is count-shaped (TRUE from the first concept-piece@v1 crossing in press_office/history.json) and its enough is three crossings, so a post is a progress report, never a fault: it gains this holds predicate, inserted exactly as follows just above PROBE = Probe(: def _holds(context: dict) -> bool: ⏎     """The trigger speaks from the first concept-piece crossing in press_office/history.json, so a ⏎     post before THREE crossings is the count growing toward enough, not a fault; this probe cannot ⏎     see a revision that failed to journal, so no single post is a failing falsifier, and a survey ⏎     that raises reads as holds False through watch_carry (835b5736bf2b child).""" ⏎     return True ; and passes carry=watch_carry(_TICKET, _carry, holds=_holds). This follows openai_wire (4c18deb605f6), whose count-toward-two post is likewise holds True. press_office sits at the repo root, not under cairn/, so the proof's _REPO_ROOT is parents[2], and press_office/ and press_office/probes/ carry no __init__.py (namespace packages; the proof imports by dotted name with the repo root on sys.path). Nothing else in a probe changes. (2) watch_carry exists in cairn/tools/base/probe.py (8ecb99998254); do not edit it. (3) Specs: each ticket's watchme spec whose probe starts with press_office/probes/ gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}, through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write. (4) Proof: press_office/proofs/test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch.py, PROVES {'b6349b1beafe': {'all': 'test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}, modeled on cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py. (5) Every proof that imports a converted probe stays green: run them.

decisions.text: D1: the probes — In each of these files under press_office/probes/: concept_piece_voyages_journal.py (eba8503cc18c: constant _TICKET — already present; holds=_holds) — append watch_carry to the existing `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line; where the constant is to be added, add `<constant> = "<its id>"` after the import block; in `PROBE = Probe(...)` replace `carry=_carry,` with `verb="watch",` and `carry=watch_carry(<constant>, _carry, <its predicate>),`. In concept_piece_voyages_journal also change to="press_office" to to="harbor_master". concept_piece_voyages_journal already holds _TICKET = "eba8503cc18c" (the 12-hex id), which watch_carry takes as its ticket; no constant is added. Its trigger is count-shaped (TRUE from the first concept-piece@v1 crossing in press_office/history.json) and its enough is three crossings, so a post is a progress report, never a fault: it gains this holds predicate, inserted exactly as follows just above PROBE = Probe(: def _holds(context: dict) -> bool: ⏎     """The trigger speaks from the first concept-piece crossing in press_office/history.json, so a ⏎     post before THREE crossings is the count growing toward enough, not a fault; this probe cannot ⏎     see a revision that failed to journal, so no single post is a failing falsifier, and a survey ⏎     that raises reads as holds False through watch_carry (835b5736bf2b child).""" ⏎     return True ; and passes carry=watch_carry(_TICKET, _carry, holds=_holds). This follows openai_wire (4c18deb605f6), whose count-toward-two post is likewise holds True. press_office sits at the repo root, not under cairn/, so the proof's _REPO_ROOT is parents[2], and press_office/ and press_office/probes/ carry no __init__.py (namespace packages; the proof imports by dotted name with the repo root on sys.path). watch_carry's signature (cairn/tools/base/probe.py): watch_carry(ticket_id: str, carry=None, *, fails=None, holds=None), exactly one of fails=/holds= given as a keyword. <its predicate> is the literal keyword argument named in the parentheses above for that file: `fails=_trigger` passes the probe's existing module-level `_trigger` function (the same one already given to Probe as trigger=), and needs no new function. `holds=_holds` passes a `_holds` function defined as stated in this decision. Each named file exists (read 2026-10-04) with a `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line and a `PROBE = Probe(...)` call holding `carry=_carry,`. Nothing else changes; watch_carry is not edited.

D2: the proof — Create press_office/proofs/test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch.py by copying the existing file cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (sealed green under 8d3c36e1fe59) byte for byte and then making ONLY these modifications: with the docstring naming press_office and ticket b6349b1beafe; PROVES = {'b6349b1beafe': {'all': 'test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}; BERTH = 'press_office/probes/'; _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] (the repo root: the directory holding cairn/); teeth renamed test_every_standing_press_office_probe_posts_watch, test_every_standing_press_office_spec_names_the_receiver and the composite test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch. Structure, in full: imports importlib, json, subprocess, sys, Path; _REPO_ROOT on sys.path; parse_workflow from cairn.tools.base.transitions; watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec; _main_tree() = Path(git -C _REPO_ROOT rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir).parent falling back to _REPO_ROOT; _tickets() = _main_tree().parent/'CairnCommons'/'tickets'; _standing() = (id, doc, spec) for each ticket whose parse_workflow(doc['workflow_and_state']).here is 'PROVED' or 'WATCHME' (a ticket that does not parse is skipped) whose watchme spec's probe starts with BERTH (every such spec: a ticket whose watchme is a list may contribute more than one tuple, and _specs() reads a dict or a list of dicts), asserting non-empty with `assert out, ...`; the posts tooth imports each probe module, takes payload = PROBE.payload({}) (Probe.payload runs the carry over that context), and asserts PROBE.verb == 'watch', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master', payload({}) carries ticket == the id, holds a bool, non-empty finding when holds is False (invariants only); the receiver tooth asserts spec['receiver'] == {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} and watchme_spec_error(doc) names no receiver fault; a __main__ block runs each, prints PASS/FAIL, exits 1 on any failure. No classes.

D3: the specs' receiver — Write one Python script file (in the session scratchpad) that does the following, and run it. Ticket files are /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json (glob '<id>-*.json', exactly one). For each of eba8503cc18c: doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text()); the watchme is a dict or list of dicts; every spec whose 'probe' starts with 'press_office/probes/' (one or several) gets spec['receiver'] = {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; then cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(p, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why='<id>: the watchme names its receiver, harbor_master\'s watch verb (b6349b1beafe)') — write(path, text, *, verb, why), text the WHOLE modified ticket. Run it as a script file (a shell command naming a record path and writing is refused by the artifact gate).

D4: green, seal, commit — Run press_office/proofs/test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (exit 0) and the probe-importing proofs (none found by grep); each must be green. Seal with `bin/cairn test --seal --timeout 900 press_office/proofs/test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch.py <the probe-importing proofs>` (it runs each and writes its validation beside it). Commit with message 'b6349b1beafe: press_office probes report to the watch' (the commit runs the reseal ladder, so allow an hour); commit the commons.

MEASURED 2026-10-04 (grep -rlnE 'concept_piece_voyages_journal|press_office(\.|/)probes' --include=*.py over the repo, excluding the probe module itself): COMPLETE SET of proofs importing /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/press_office/probes/ is EMPTY — no file imports it, so the seal command names only the new proof press_office/proofs/test_press_office_probes_report_to_the_watch.py; the one existing proof, press_office/proofs/test_concept_piece_voyage.py, does not import the probe and is resealed by the commit's ladder if its fingerprint moves.
